title: Onboarding Handback and First-90-Days Operational Guide
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Summary

This document defines the technical handback process and the operational expectations for the first 90 days after an enterprise customer goes live on Redwood Inference (hosted or Dedicated). It is intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineering (SE), Onboarding Engineers, and the L2 oncall team.

Scope

- Applies to enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments and enterprise-level Hosted integrations that require an SE handover.
- Covers: handoff checklist, SLA matrix, runbook entries for common post-go-live issues, escalation steps, monitoring baseline, and QBR readiness checklist for the first 90 days.

Goals and success metrics (first 90 days)

- Availability SLO: 99.95% per calendar month for production inference endpoints.
- Latency SLO: P95 request-to-first-token < 300 ms for short-text generation workloads (<= 256 tokens) on Dedicated pools.
- Error budget: < 0.05% failed requests (5xx) attributable to Redwood services. Customer-side errors (4xx) excluded.
- Onboarding health: 80% of customer-defined success criteria met by day 30, 95% by day 90.
- QBR readiness: onboarding artifacts, traffic profile, cost trends, and open action items delivered two weeks before the 90-day review.

Handback checklist (must be completed before formal handoff)

1) Contractual & access items (owner: CSM)
   1. Confirm customer account and billing profile in Finance (billing contact verified).
   2. Verify list of whitelisted IPs, VPC peering, or VPN endpoints (for Dedicated/Private).
   3. Confirm KMS/HSM key rotation schedule and access for logs/audit.

2) Technical verification (owner: SE / Onboarding Engineer)
   1. Baseline performance test completed: runbench report attached and passing acceptance criteria (attach: runbench-<customer>-v1.json).
   2. Model versions pinned and documented (model-id, quantization profile if any).
   3. Ingress/egress networking validated: HTTPS termination, MTU checks, and route tables.
   4. Observability hooks installed: metrics, ingest for traces, and token-level cost tagging enabled.

3) Operational readiness (owner: Oncall + CSM)
   1. Oncall runbooks created for the customer under team wiki (link to runbook entry).
   2. Alerting thresholds verified (see SLA matrix below).
   3. Access matrix for customer ops and Redwood SRE/SE is finalized (least privilege).

Operational SLA matrix (reference thresholds and owners)

| Area | SLO / Threshold | Primary owner | Escalation target |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Endpoint availability | 99.95% monthly | Customer Success (CSM) / SE | SRE oncall within 30m |
| P95 latency (<=256 tokens) | < 300 ms (Dedicated) | SE / Runtime team | Runtime oncall within 60m |
| Error rate (5xx) | < 0.05% | Runtime team | SRE within 30m |
| Cold-start median | < 1200 ms | Runtime team | Engineering within 2h |
| Cost anomaly | < 25% deviation vs forecast | Finance + CSM | Growth/RevOps notified 1 business day |

Note: thresholds above are targets agreed during onboarding and may be tuned per-contract. All alerts should map to the customer-specific alerting policy in PagerDuty and Slack channel.

Escalation & handoff timeline (high level)

- Day 0 (Go-live): SE oncall and CSM present. Monitor first 24 hours for errors and latency regressions.
- Day 1–7: Daily sync between CSM, SE, and SRE for the first-week incidents and visibility.
- Day 8–30: Bi-weekly operational check-ins, performance tuning (batching/KV cache config), and cost review.
- Day 31–90: Weekly check-ins until SLA stability and customer success criteria are met; prepare QBR artifacts by day 75.

Handoff procedure (detailed, numbered)

1. Pre-handoff readiness demo (SE + customer): run the baseline load test (recommended: k6 or locust harness) and demonstrate acceptance criteria.
2. Fill the Onboarding Runbook template: include endpoints, model pins, route policies, alerting, and contact matrix.
3. Create customer-specific monitoring dashboard: tokens-per-minute, p95 latency, 5xx rate, cost-by-route. Share read-only link with customer.
4. Add the customer to the SRE PagerDuty rotation as a secondary for the first 30 days.
5. Formal handoff meeting: CSM presents business context, SE presents technical state, SRE presents monitoring/alerts. Capture action items in Jira and assign owners.

Post-handoff runbook excerpts (copy these into the customer runbook)

- Immediate checks when an alert fires:
  - Step 1: Verify if alert is customer-generated (4xx) vs platform (5xx) by checking trace id and edge logs.
  - Step 2: If platform (5xx), run diagnostic command: curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood.example/v1/engines/<engine-id>/health || cat /var/log/runtime/errors.log (SE only).
  - Step 3: Check KV cache hit rate and batching stats from /metrics endpoint (prometheus name: redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio). Thresholds: < 60% indicates mis-priming.
  - Step 4: Escalate per matrix (see table above) and create a postmortem if the incident causes > 30m downtime affecting > 10% of requests.

Common post-go-live issues and mitigations

- High P95 latency after deployment:
  - Likely causes: non-optimal batching, model quantization fallback, and warmup not run.
  - Mitigation steps: confirm batching policy in route config, enable prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts, trigger a lightweight warmup job: POST /internal/warmup {"engine":"<engine-id>","samples":10}.

- Increased token spend vs forecast:
  - Likely causes: prompt inflation, unexpected retries, or high token-per-request usage.
  - Mitigation steps: enable token-limit policy on the route, add request logging with sampling to capture outlier prompts, review SDK integration to verify retries/backoff.

- Frequent 429s (rate limit) during ramp:
  - Likely causes: client-side concurrency and missing client-side rate limiting.
  - Mitigation: apply client-side leaky-bucket throttling; coordinate with SE to provision burst capacity for first 48 hours.

Monitoring & instrumentation checklist (must be visible in the first 24 hours)

- Dashboards: Tokens/minute, per-route cost, p95 latency, 5xx rate, KV cache hit ratio.
- Traces: sample 1% of requests with full request/response payload for the first 7 days. Ensure PII redaction enabled.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with request_id, trace_id, route, model_id. Retention: 90 days by default for enterprise customers.

CLI and example snippets

- Fetch engine health:
  - Example: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/engines/my-prod-engine/health

- Warmup job (cURL example):
  - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"engine":"my-prod-engine","samples":["Hello","Summarize: short text"],"concurrency":2}' https://api.redwood.example/internal/warmup

- Sample route config (JSON fragment to include in onboarding runbook):
  - {
      "route_name": "customer-a-default",
      "engine": "my-prod-engine",
      "batching": { "max_batch_tokens": 1024, "max_batch_size": 32 },
      "cache": { "prefix_cache": true, "kv_profile": "high-hit" },
      "slo_tags": ["enterprise-2026"],
      "rate_limits": { "requests_per_minute": 1200 }
    }

QBR readiness checklist (to deliver by day 75)

- Usage trends and cost breakdown (token-level) for day 0–75.
- Performance baseline vs current (p50/p95/p99).
- Open incidents and remediation items.
- Proposed optimization roadmap (batching/cache/quantizaton) with estimated cost impact.

Owner & contacts

- Onboarding SE: name & email (populate in runbook).
- Customer Success Manager: name & email (populate in runbook).
- Runtime Oncall: rotas listed in Ops PagerDuty.

Appendix: Acceptance test checklist (sample commands)

1. Latency smoke test (10 concurrent requests): run k6 script; expected p95 < configured threshold.
2. Fault injection: simulate a dropped node and verify automatic fallback to other capacity pools within 60s.
3. Cost smoke test: replay representative traffic for 1 hour and measure tokens-per-minute vs forecast.

Notes and links

- Attach: baseline runbench JSON, onboarding runbook template, SLA addendum (if different from platform defaults).
- For security-sensitive customers, coordinate with Security & Compliance for audit logging and evidence packages.

If you have questions about any step, ping #cs-onboarding or open a ticket in the Onboarding queue.
